plugins.name: Donor Merchant – Donation Form with Recurring Donations, Stripe and PayPal
plugins.author: Matt McWilliam
plugins.short_description: Free donation plugin for nonprofits, churches and charities: one-time and recurring donations with Stripe and PayPal, donor portal and receipts.
plugins.description:
Donor Merchant is a free donation plugin for WordPress. It gives a nonprofit, church, charity, school, or community group a donation form that takes one-time and recurring donations through Stripe and PayPal, keeps a record of every donor and gift in your own database, and sends receipts.

Try the live demo: pick an amount, choose monthly, cover the fees, and see the receipt. Nothing is charged.

Every feature is in the free plugin. There are no paid add-ons, no locked settings, and no fee added on top of what Stripe or PayPal charge. Optional paid support plans are available: priority email help for a single organization, or faster help for agencies looking after several client sites. Details are at donormerchant.com/pricing.

Who it is for

  • Small nonprofits and charities that need a dependable donation page without a monthly platform bill.
  • Churches taking online tithes and offerings, with funds such as General, Building, or Missions, and year-end giving statements donors can download themselves.
  • Schools, PTAs, booster clubs, animal rescues, and community groups running a goal-based campaign.
  • Freelancers and agencies who build sites for nonprofit clients and want one donation setup they can repeat on every site, with no license keys.

Donations

  • One-time and recurring donations. Donors choose one-time, weekly, every 2 weeks, monthly, quarterly, or yearly, and you pick which of those your form offers. Recurring giving works on both gateways: Stripe subscriptions and PayPal subscriptions.
  • Stripe through Stripe’s Payment Element: cards, plus Apple Pay and Google Pay where you have them turned on in your Stripe account.
  • Bank debit (ACH) from US bank accounts through Stripe, as a setting you switch on.
  • PayPal Smart Buttons for one-time gifts.
  • 20 currencies, with WooCommerce-style number formatting: currency position, thousand and decimal separators, and number of decimals, used on the form, receipts, statements, and reports.
  • Suggested amounts and a minimum. Your own suggested amounts, a custom amount field, and a minimum donation the server enforces.
  • Fee recovery. Donors can choose to add the processing fee to their gift, worked out from the percentage and fixed fee you enter so that the full gift is left after the processor’s cut. A donor who pays a one-time gift by bank account is asked for the lower bank fee instead.
  • Designations. Donors pick the fund their gift supports.
  • Tributes. A gift can be made in honor of or in memory of someone, with an optional message.
  • Employer matching. An optional question asks whether the donor’s employer matches gifts. The employer shows on the donation, your new-donation email and the donor’s receipt.
  • Custom fields. Add your own questions as text, paragraph, dropdown, or checkbox fields, each required or optional.
  • Test mode. Test end to end with Stripe test keys and the PayPal sandbox before going live.

Gift Aid for UK charities

Offer Gift Aid on the form when your currency is pounds sterling. Donors tick HMRC’s model declaration (unticked by default) and give a house name or number and postcode, or a full address if they live outside the UK. One declaration covers future gifts and gifts in the past 4 years, so monthly donors are covered. The declaration is stored exactly as the donor saw it.

Donor Merchant > Gift Aid lists the gifts ready to claim and downloads them in HMRC’s schedule format, ready to paste into HMRC’s spreadsheet for Charities Online. Mark gifts as claimed so they are never claimed twice, see refunds that need reporting back, and cancel a declaration when a donor asks. Donors can also cancel from the donor portal.

Campaigns and goal thermometers

Create as many campaigns as you need, each with its own goal, description, suggested amounts, and an optional end date after which its form stops taking gifts. A campaign’s form shows progress toward the goal, and the [donor_merchant_progress campaign="N"] shortcode places the same thermometer anywhere else on your site.

Donor records and reports

  • Every donor and gift is saved in your WordPress database, with each donor’s lifetime total and last donation date.
  • A dashboard shows total raised, this month’s total, number of donations and donors, recurring gifts, and the average gift.
  • Search and filter the donations list by status, and export donations or donors to CSV.
  • Record offline gifts (check, cash, bank transfer, or other) so your totals stay complete, or let donors choose “check or bank transfer” on the form: they get your instructions, and you mark the gift received when it arrives.
  • Add a donor by hand, and correct a gift’s status to completed, refunded, or failed without deleting it. Corrections never email the donor.
  • An optional monthly fundraising summary is emailed to you on the first of each month.

Receipts, statements, and the donor portal

  • Email customization like WooCommerce’s: every email the plugin sends (donation receipt, recurring gift receipt, offline gift instructions, failed recurring payment, new-donation alert, donor portal link and monthly summary) can be switched on or off, given its own subject, heading and message with placeholders such as {first_name}, {amount} and {designation}, and sent as HTML or plain text. Add your logo, colors, font and footer, set the From name and address, preview each email live on desktop or mobile, and send yourself a test.
  • A printable receipt for every gift, showing your organization’s address, tax ID, and your own receipt wording. Donors save it as a PDF from their browser, so no PDF library is bundled.
  • Annual giving statements for the current and previous year.
  • A donor portal with passwordless sign-in by one-time email link, where donors see their giving history, open receipts and statements, cancel any recurring gift and update the card on a Stripe one, with no setup needed in Stripe. Receipts for recurring gifts link to the portal, and you can also cancel a donor’s recurring gift from the Donations list.

Donation importer

The built-in donation importer reads a CSV export and recognizes the exports from GiveWP, Charitable, Donorbox, PayPal, Stripe, WooCommerce, Gravity Forms, and WPForms. Any other spreadsheet works too.

You confirm which column is which before anything is written, and a preview shows the result first. Re-running is safe: gifts already on file are matched by transaction ID, or by donor, amount, and date. Imported gifts never send receipts or fire integrations, and rows marked as test mode can be skipped. Each file can hold up to 10,000 rows.

Integrations

  • Mailchimp. Add donors to an audience, with a “keep me updated” checkbox on the form and optional double opt-in.
  • Outgoing webhooks. Send completed donations to Zapier, Make, a CRM, or your own code. Each request is signed with HMAC-SHA256 so the receiver can confirm it came from your site.

Design and placement

  • A Donation Form block, plus the shortcodes [donor_merchant], [donor_merchant campaign="N"], [donor_merchant_progress campaign="N"], and [donor_merchant_portal]. A Shortcodes tab in Settings lists each one with your campaign IDs filled in, ready to copy.
  • Six accent colors or a custom color, and three button shapes (pill, rounded, sharp), with a live preview in Settings.
  • Your own wording: switch “donation” and “donate” to “gift” and “give”, or to your own words, everywhere donors see them, and reword any other text with a simple replacement table.

Records that match your processor

Renewals, refunds, and bank payments that settle days later are recorded from Stripe’s and PayPal’s signed webhooks, so the donations list lines up with your gateway account. A partial refund leaves the gift in your totals, and only a full refund marks it refunded.

How it stays secure

Payment details are collected by Stripe and PayPal directly in the donor’s browser. No card number, expiration date, or CVC is ever transmitted to or stored on your server. Donation totals are recomputed on the server, payment status is confirmed server-to-gateway, and webhook signatures are verified.

Card testing and spam are handled without a CAPTCHA by default: a hidden honeypot field, a signed check that rejects forms submitted impossibly fast, per-IP rate limiting, and a server-side minimum amount. If your payment processor asks you to add a CAPTCHA, the donor_merchant_pre_donation filter lets you plug one in without editing the plugin.

What it does not do

Donor Merchant has no peer-to-peer fundraising, text-to-give, matching-gift company lookup, or drag-and-drop form builder. Forms are set up from the Settings screens.

External services

To process donations this plugin connects to third-party payment and (optionally) marketing services. Nothing is sent until you enable and configure a given service.

  • Stripe (only when Stripe is enabled). The Stripe.js library is loaded from https://js.stripe.com on pages that display the donation form, so payment details can be collected securely in the donor’s browser. Your server also calls the Stripe API at https://api.stripe.com to create payment intents, customers, and subscriptions, and to verify payments. Data sent: donation amount and currency, the donor’s name, email and phone number if given, an internal reference for the donation, and the payment details the donor enters (handled by Stripe – they do not touch your server). Stripe terms: https://stripe.com/legal – privacy: https://stripe.com/privacy
  • PayPal (only when PayPal is enabled). The PayPal JS SDK is loaded from https://www.paypal.com on pages with the donation form. Your server calls the PayPal API (https://api-m.paypal.com, or https://api-m.sandbox.paypal.com in sandbox mode) to create and capture orders and subscriptions. Data sent: donation amount, currency, and an internal reference. PayPal terms: https://www.paypal.com/legalhub – privacy: https://www.paypal.com/privacy
  • Mailchimp (optional – only when you enable it). By default the form shows a “keep me updated” checkbox and only opted-in donors are sent. If you switch that checkbox off in the settings, every donor is added to the audience, so leave it on unless you have another basis for contacting them. Your server calls the Mailchimp API (https://<dc>.api.mailchimp.com) to add the donor to the audience you choose. Data sent: donor email and name. Mailchimp terms: https://mailchimp.com/legal/terms/ – privacy: https://mailchimp.com/legal/privacy/
  • Outgoing webhooks (optional). If you enter one or more webhook URLs, completed-donation data is POSTed to those URLs – which you control and choose (e.g. your Zapier or Make endpoint). No third party receives data unless you configure it.

Getting started

  1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Go to Donor Merchant → Settings → Payments and paste your Stripe and/or PayPal API keys.
  3. Add the Donation Form block (or [donor_merchant]) to any page.
  4. If you accept recurring gifts, add the webhook URL shown on the Payments tab to your Stripe or PayPal account.
  5. Test with Stripe test mode or the PayPal sandbox, then switch to live.

plugins.name: Blazo Checkout
plugins.author: Blazo Checkout
plugins.short_description: Your WooCommerce checkout is losing you money. Blazo recovers abandoned carts, upsells every order, and shows you exactly what it earned.
plugins.description:
Seven in ten shoppers who reach checkout leave without buying. That’s not a traffic problem — it’s a checkout problem. Blazo Checkout replaces your WooCommerce checkout with a hosted one built to close the sale, win back the ones who almost didn’t, and sell them a little more on the way out.

Here’s what changes the day you install it:

Fewer carts die at checkout

A faster, cleaner, trust-built checkout page — guest-first, mobile-tuned, no surprise costs at the last step. Every field on it exists because it earns its place.

Built for speed, not just for looks

Your branding and settings load from the edge network first, falling back to the API only if needed. Cities and delivery offices load from the API first, falling back to the edge if it’s slow. Order completion tries the API first, then the edge network as a backup. Every step has a fallback, so shoppers never wait on a single point of failure.

It stays up even when your site doesn’t

If your store goes down mid-checkout, the order isn’t lost — Blazo holds it and pushes it into WooCommerce the second your site is back. And if your courier’s API goes down (it happens more than anyone admits — cities and pickup offices just vanish from checkout, and the sale goes with them), Blazo already has that data cached on its own servers. Your checkout keeps working. Your customer never finds out there was a problem.

Abandoned carts come back to life — on every channel

Someone bails before paying? Blazo follows up by email, SMS, Viber, Telegram, WhatsApp, or a phone call — whichever gets a real human to finish the order. Revenue you were already writing off as lost.

Every order gets bigger

Order bumps at checkout and post-purchase offers, placed exactly where shoppers are most willing to say yes. (Post-purchase upsells: coming soon.)

A thank-you page that keeps working after the sale

Order summary, delivery status, tracking, “contact support” — all one click away, right after purchase. Fewer “where’s my order” tickets, more customers who trust you enough to come back.

You see the money, not just the orders

A dashboard built around one number: how much Blazo actually made you — recovered carts, upsells, and the conversion lift, broken out and dated. No spreadsheets, no guessing.

Test what actually converts

Run steps vs. one-page checkout head-to-head and let the data decide. More test types are coming.

Make it look and behave like your checkout

Style it to match your brand, and set exactly which fields are required and which aren’t. Field hide/reorder controls are coming next.

Know which orders are actually going to ship

Every customer gets a risk score — critical wherever cash-on-delivery is the default payment method, because a refused COD parcel means you pay courier fees both ways for nothing.

Sell printed and digital side by side

Selling a book as both print and e-book? Shoppers switch between the versions right in the checkout with one click — no trip back to the product page. Digital products (virtual or downloadable in WooCommerce) are recognised automatically: cash on delivery is hidden for them, and an order with only digital items skips the delivery step entirely — no courier, no shipping charge, no address to type.

Built for real-world delivery, wherever you sell

Courier selection, pickup-office lookup, cash-on-delivery, B2B company/EIK fields — the messy logistics details that lose sales when a generic checkout gets them wrong. Deep support for Central & Eastern European delivery out of the box.

Make it yours, top to bottom

Run checkout on your own custom domain. Every word on the page is translatable, so shoppers never feel like they left your store.

Your order statuses, everywhere they matter

The custom statuses you define in Blazo show up in WooCommerce with the right name — in the admin, and on the customer’s My Account > Orders screen too. They keep their names even if the API is unreachable, and they appear in your admin language. Create a waybill and the order moves to the status you mapped instantly, right there on the order screen. Once an order is with the courier it’s locked from editing, so line items can’t drift away from the waybill already printed.

Set up once, never touch again

Connect with a single onboarding token. No copying API keys or secrets by hand. Your custom order statuses sync automatically. Every order lands back in WooCommerce — customer, address, shipping, fees, all of it — the moment it’s confirmed.

Bank-grade by default

Every checkout payload is AES-256-GCM encrypted and HMAC-signed. Every confirmation is signature-verified, replay-protected, and de-duplicated. Order totals are checked against what the shopper actually confirmed, so price tampering gets caught, not shipped.

Coming soon

In-house heatmap tracking, so you see exactly how shoppers move through your checkout — no third-party script required. And a dedicated order-tracking page with its own upsell placements, so the sale doesn’t stop at “thank you.”

Full feature list

  • Hosted checkout that replaces native WooCommerce checkout — redirect and done.
  • Edge-first loading with automatic API fallback for branding, delivery data, and order completion.
  • Offline resilience: orders and courier data are held and synced automatically if your site or your courier’s API goes down.
  • Abandoned cart recovery via email, SMS, Viber, Telegram, WhatsApp, or phone call.
  • Order bumps at checkout (post-purchase upsells coming soon).
  • Branded post-purchase thank-you page with order status, tracking, and support links.
  • Revenue dashboard: recovered revenue, upsell revenue, conversion lift, all in one view.
  • A/B testing between step and one-page checkout (more test types coming).
  • Custom styling, with control over which fields are required.
  • Per-customer risk scoring, purpose-built for cash-on-delivery markets.
  • Courier + pickup office selection, cash-on-delivery, B2B company/EIK fields.
  • Custom checkout domain support.
  • Fully translatable checkout.
  • Custom order status sync from Blazo into WooCommerce — localised names, shown on the customer’s My Account screen as well as in the admin, and kept through API outages.
  • Waybill creation moves the order to its mapped status immediately, on the order screen.
  • Orders in a Blazo custom status are locked from editing, so line items can’t diverge from a printed waybill.
  • Waybill number shown prominently on the order screen with one-click copy.
  • Zero-touch onboarding via one-time token.
  • AES-256-GCM encryption + HMAC signing on every payload.
  • HMAC-verified, replay-protected, idempotent order confirmation.
  • Order-total tampering detection.
  • High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS) compatible.
  • Configurable order status mapping: which status new orders get (by delivery and payment method), which status each event pushes, and how WooCommerce statuses map back.
  • Coming soon: in-house heatmap tracking, and a dedicated order-tracking page with upsell placements.

A Blazo account is required. This plugin is the connector — the checkout itself, the recovery engine, and the dashboard live on Blazo’s platform.

External services

This plugin relies on the Blazo Checkout third-party service to function. It is not usable without a Blazo account, and by installing it you direct your store’s checkout traffic to Blazo.

What is sent, and when

  1. At checkout (browser redirect). When a shopper clicks “Proceed to checkout”, the plugin builds an order payload and redirects the shopper’s browser to your configured Blazo checkout URL. The payload is AES-256-GCM encrypted and HMAC-signed and contains: store ID, currency, return/callback URLs, cart line items (product name, SKU, price, quantity, image URL, variation data), order totals, and the customer’s email, first name and last name and, if they are logged in, their WordPress user ID (where available). Each line also carries its category IDs, brand, whether the product is virtual, downloadable or needs shipping, and cart-item keys so bundled items stay linked to their bundle. When the shopper comes from the instalment calculator on a product page, it also carries the chosen PB Personal Finance programme and down payment.

  2. On connection (server to server). When the merchant connects the store, the plugin sends a one-time onboarding token and the site URL to the Blazo API (/plugin/bootstrap) to retrieve the store configuration.

  3. Order confirmation (server to server). Blazo calls back to this site to create the order. No store-initiated PII is sent in this step; the plugin receives and verifies the confirmed order data. If your site is unreachable when Blazo tries to deliver an order, Blazo holds it and retries automatically once your site is back up.

  4. Status sync (server to server). The plugin periodically requests your custom order-status definitions from the Blazo API.

  5. Customer accounts (server to server, from Blazo to your site). When a shopper logs in or creates an account in Blazo Checkout, Blazo sends their email address (and, for a login, the password they typed) to signed endpoints on your site. The password is checked by WordPress and is never stored by Blazo. Your site answers with the customer’s ID, name, email, phone and saved billing and shipping addresses so the checkout can be prefilled. Only when the matching WooCommerce “Accounts & Privacy” settings are enabled.

  6. Instalment offers on product pages (server to server). On single product pages of stores that offer PB Personal Finance credit through Blazo, your site asks the Blazo API (/plugin/bnp/widget) for the bank’s instalment offers. It sends the store ID, product ID, variation ID, quantity, price, down payment and the product’s category IDs. No shopper data is sent. Answers are cached on your site for a few minutes.

Service endpoints

  • Checkout URL — configured by the merchant (e.g. https://checkout.blazo.bg, or your own custom domain)
  • API base URL — configured by the merchant (e.g. https://api.blazo.bg)

Service provider, terms and privacy

  • Service provided by Blazo (a product of Fantasy Software Ltd) — https://blazo.bg
  • Terms of Service — https://blazo.bg/terms
  • Privacy Policy — https://blazo.bg/privacy

Merchants are responsible for disclosing this data flow to their own customers as required by applicable privacy law.

plugins.name: AI Soft – AI Auto Post Publisher Lite
plugins.author: Tauhidul Hossain Tanmoy
plugins.short_description: Generate WordPress drafts from a source URL, pasted text, or a topic to discover, using your own AI provider key. Categories, SEO fields, images.
plugins.description:
AI Soft – AI Auto Post Publisher Lite helps you turn a source URL, pasted text, or a topic into a structured WordPress draft, using your own API key from Gemini, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, or Claude.

It is built to work with any WordPress site and any public post type, not just one kind of content. A job posting, a news update, a blog article, a business page, a product review, or a how-to guide are all detected and structured appropriately.

Main features

  • Bring your own AI provider key: Gemini, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, or Claude. Gemini, OpenRouter, and Groq all offer a free tier to get started.
  • Generate a draft from a source URL, pasted text, or by discovering trending topics.
  • Works with any public post type on your site, not only the built-in Post type.
  • One-click category presets for common website types (news/magazine, job board, blog, business, education, and more), fully editable, with an option to override which taxonomy a post type uses.
  • Automatic trending-topic discovery per category, with optional region and trusted-source focus, plus a daily auto-publish schedule.
  • Local featured images generated automatically, with the option to use a source image instead.
  • SEO fields (title, meta description, focus keyword) and automatic category/tag assignment.
  • A Default Author setting so scheduled and discovered posts are always assigned a real author.
  • A short interactive guided tour on every settings screen.
  • A Content Optimizer to analyze and improve the SEO/content quality of existing posts and pages.

Bring your own key

This plugin does not include any AI service of its own and does not phone home anywhere for content generation. You provide your own API key for whichever provider you choose, and requests go directly from your WordPress site to that provider. See “External services” below for exactly what is sent and where.

Everything is included

Every feature — draft generation, topic discovery, the daily auto publisher, images, SEO fields, category presets and the Content Optimizer — works with any supported provider. Nothing is locked, nothing is time-limited, and there is no upgrade to buy.

Gemini, OpenRouter, and Groq have free tiers, so you can run the plugin at no cost. OpenAI and Claude are billed by usage by those companies; the plugin treats all five the same and uses whichever keys you have saved.

External services

This plugin connects to third-party services in order to generate content. It does not send any data to these services unless you actively use the corresponding feature.

AI provider (required to generate content)

You choose one AI provider in Settings and enter your own API key for it. When you generate a draft, the plugin sends your source text/URL content and your site’s brief description (from the Universal Website Profile) to that provider’s API, and receives back the generated draft. No data is sent unless you click Generate, run Topic Discovery, run the daily Auto Publisher, or use the Content Optimizer.

  • Google Gemini — https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms — Privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • OpenAI — https://openai.com/api/policies/service-terms/ — Privacy policy: https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy
  • OpenRouter — https://openrouter.ai/terms — Privacy policy: https://openrouter.ai/privacy
  • Groq — https://groq.com/terms-of-use — Privacy policy: https://groq.com/privacy-policy
  • Anthropic Claude — https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms — Privacy policy: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy

Live model list sync (automatic when a key is saved)

To keep each provider’s model dropdown current, the plugin periodically calls that provider’s own model-listing endpoint (no content, just your API key) once you have saved a key for it: Google’s v1beta/models, OpenAI’s v1/models, Groq’s v1/models, and Anthropic’s v1/models. OpenRouter’s v1/models is also queried and does not require a key. This happens the first time you view Settings after saving a key, once daily in the background, and when you click “Refresh Models Now.” See the provider links above for terms/privacy.

Search phrase suggestions (optional, on by default)

While “Google Keyword Expansion” is enabled in Settings, the plugin sends a category’s seed topic to Google’s public autocomplete endpoint before a Topic Discovery or Auto Publisher run, so discovery can search the phrasings people actually type. Only the seed topic text and your configured content language and target country are sent; no API key, no post content, and no site or visitor data. Results are cached for a day. Turning the setting off stops these requests entirely.

  • Google autocomplete (https://suggestqueries.google.com) — Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms — Privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Source page discovery via public search feeds (on by default)

Unless “Discovery Source” is set to “AI providers only”, the plugin finds candidate source pages by reading Bing’s public search RSS feeds — https://www.bing.com/search?...&format=rss and https://www.bing.com/news/search?...&format=rss — before, or instead of, asking an AI provider to search the web. This needs no API key and no account. Only the search phrase is sent, built from the category’s topic plus your configured content language and target country; no API key, no post content, and no site or visitor data. Results are cached for three hours. Setting “Discovery Source” to “AI providers only” stops these requests entirely.

  • Bing search (https://www.bing.com) — Terms: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/ — Privacy policy: https://privacy.microsoft.com/en-us/privacystatement

Source URL fetching (optional)

If you paste a source URL when generating a draft, the plugin fetches that page’s public content directly from your WordPress server so it can be used as source material. This only happens for URLs you provide.

Image lookups (optional)

If a source image or reference image URL is provided, or an image search is used to find a relevant supporting image, the plugin may fetch images from the site hosting them, or from Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org, no account/key required), to download into your Media Library. This only happens when the corresponding image feature is enabled and in use.

  • Wikimedia Commons — Terms of use: https://foundation.wikimedia.org/wiki/Policy:Terms_of_Use — Privacy policy: https://foundation.wikimedia.org/wiki/Policy:Privacy_policy

If you enter an Unsplash or Pexels API key in Settings, the plugin searches that service for a relevant real photograph before falling back to Wikimedia Commons. This only happens when a key is configured.

  • Unsplash — API guidelines: https://help.unsplash.com/en/articles/2511245-unsplash-api-guidelines — Licence terms: https://help.unsplash.com/en/collections/1463188-unsplash-license — Privacy policy (Unsplash is a Getty Images company): https://www.gettyimages.com/company/privacy-policy
  • Pexels — https://www.pexels.com/api/documentation/#api-terms-of-use — Privacy policy: https://www.pexels.com/privacy-policy/

If you enter a Google API key and Programmable Search Engine ID in Settings, the plugin sends the post’s image search terms to Google’s Custom Search JSON API to find a relevant photograph, and downloads the selected image into your Media Library. This only happens when both values are configured.

  • Google Programmable Search — https://developers.google.com/custom-search/v1/site_restricted_api — Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms — Privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

AI-generated images (optional)

If you enable “AI image fallback” in Settings and no real photo can be found, the plugin sends a short text prompt describing the post’s topic to OpenAI’s image generation API (using the OpenAI key entered above) and downloads the resulting image into your Media Library. This only happens when this setting is enabled and no real photo was found. See the OpenAI terms/privacy policy links above.

plugins.name: RadarAddress – Checkout Address Autocomplete for WooCommerce

plugins.short_description: Fewer parcels sent back: customers pick their real address at checkout, and wrong addresses are flagged before you ship. Never blocks an order.
plugins.description:
A parcel that comes back because of a wrong street, a missing house number or the wrong postcode costs you the shipping twice and a customer who waits. RadarAddress catches the mistake at checkout, while the customer is typing, and flags the orders whose address still does not check out, before you ship.

RadarAddress completes and corrects the customer’s address while they type it at checkout — billing and shipping, classic checkout and Checkout Block — in the countries where the national address register is in service (Italy, Germany, France, Spain, the Netherlands, Belgium, Austria, Switzerland, Denmark, Norway, Finland, Iceland, Portugal and more). The postcode and the house number come from the register at the moment of selection; the customer can always change what they wrote. Nothing ever blocks the order.

Every new order is checked on the server: outcome and verified form are saved next to the order, the order list shows a colour dot (verified, warning, to review, not verified) with a filter, and the order screen shows the verified address with one button to apply it. The order address is never changed by itself.

What you get

  • Address autocomplete on billing and shipping, classic checkout and Checkout Block.
  • Correction on the field of an address typed by hand (postcode, city, street) — optional.
  • Verification of every order, with the verified address, coordinates and the reason.
  • «To review» flag, filter and bulk action in the order list.
  • Verification of existing orders that you choose: which statuses, from which date, newest or oldest first, all of them, only the first ones, or a few at a time every month with a subscription.
  • Verification precision from strict to maximum: how far RadarAddress goes to find an address written badly.
  • Fail-open by design: if RadarAddress does not answer, the checkout goes on as usual.
  • Data stays in the EU. Sources: the national address registers, published as open data.

How it works

  1. Create a free account on radaraddress.com (every month 50 contact checks are free).
  2. Create an API token in your personal area.
  3. Paste it in WooCommerce → Settings → RadarAddress and press «Verify and save».

Typing is free. One contact check is used when the customer selects an address, or when an order is verified — one per address, never twice for the same one. For a small shop the 50 free checks a month are often all it needs; beyond that, packs and monthly subscriptions on radaraddress.com.

Third-party service

This plugin sends the address typed at checkout and the order addresses to the RadarAddress API (https://www.radaraddress.com) to get suggestions and verification results. Terms: https://www.radaraddress.com/en/terms — Privacy: https://www.radaraddress.com/en/privacy-policy.php

External services

This plugin connects to the RadarAddress API, a service run by RadarWave (the author of this plugin), to suggest and verify postal addresses. It does nothing until you paste your own API token in WooCommerce > Settings > RadarAddress.

  • What is sent and when: while a customer types an address at checkout, the text typed in the address fields (street, house number, postcode, city, country) is sent to the API to get suggestions; when an order is placed, or when you verify existing orders from the admin, the order’s billing and shipping address (name, company, street, postcode, city, province, country) is sent to be verified. Your API token is sent with every request to identify your account. With each request the plugin also sends the address of the checkout page (without its query string) and which form and part it comes from (for example checkout/billing), so the request can be found in your service log. The settings page also asks the API for your account’s remaining verifications.
  • Where: https://www.radaraddress.com/api/v1/ (calls are made by your site’s server, or through the plugin’s own REST endpoint on your site: the token never reaches the browser).
  • Terms of use: https://www.radaraddress.com/en/terms
  • Privacy policy: https://www.radaraddress.com/en/privacy-policy

plugins.name: DadsFam Login Security
plugins.author: dadsfam
plugins.short_description: Stops brute-force attacks with its own self-learning Brain that knows your real people, locks bots out fast and fixes its own setup.
plugins.description:
DadsFam Login Security protects the most-attacked part of your WordPress site — the login form — without making you read a manual or fiddle with servers.

Most login plugins count wrong passwords and lock out whoever hits the number. That works on bots, and it also locks out your customer who mistyped twice on the same office connection a bot happens to be using. Version 2.0 gives the plugin its own Brain, running entirely on your site, so it can tell the two apart.

The Brain (free, and it never phones home)

  • Ask the Brain. Type a question the way you would ask a person — “is my site safe?”, “why can’t Sarah sign in?”, then “unlock her”; “how many attacks this month?”, then “and last month?” — and it answers from your own site’s data with the numbers, a small chart and the fix as one button. It forgives typos, answers in Afrikaans when you ask in Afrikaans, explains every feature, and lives on your dashboard and the WordPress dashboard. Its own language engine runs on your site; nothing is sent to an AI service.
  • Lost phone? One sentence. “Who is signed in right now?” or “sign Sarah out of every device”.
  • A heat-map of when attacks come, and a diary of everything the Brain did by itself.
  • The Brain’s weekly letter (optional): its plain-English story of the week, emailed every Monday.
  • It learns your real people. Every correct password teaches it what a real sign-in on your site looks like. Every attempt on a username that does not exist teaches it what a bot looks like. It only learns from facts, never from its own guesses.
  • It checks its own work. When a real person it had doubted signs in, it notes the mistake; twice in a month and it demands more certainty before it acts.
  • It learns which usernames only bots use. Once several different addresses try a name nobody on your site has, one try is enough to lock them out — never on a network your people use.
  • It learns from DadsFam AntiSpam. An address caught spamming your forms is treated with suspicion if it then tries to sign in.
  • It shows which real accounts are being guessed, and tells the week’s story in plain English.
  • A browser that has signed in before is never locked out by its address. Its typos do not count, even on a shared connection that is being attacked. (After a generous number of misses the normal rules apply again, in case a laptop is stolen.)
  • Obvious bots are locked out on the first try — but only when it is almost certain and two hard clues agree, like a script with no browser posting straight at the form. A real browser cannot trip it.
  • Every attempt is explained in plain words: “97% bot: posted straight at the sign-in form without opening it, no language setting.”
  • Autopilot. During an attack it raises the shields (strangers get half the tries and a longer time-out), keeps whole attacking networks away for a day, then three, then a week — and lowers everything again once it is quiet. Networks your people use are never touched.
  • Unlock by email. A locked-out person can email themselves a one-time unlock link. It only ever goes to the account’s own email address.
  • Self-repair. Every day and after every update it checks its own setup and fixes what is safe to fix — like the Cloudflare setting that lets one bot lock everybody out — then tells you what it did.
  • Remote control. On WordPress 6.9+ every action is available as a WordPress Ability, so an assistant you trust can check your login security or let someone back in.

Everything else you get (free)

  • Smart lockouts — after too many wrong passwords an address is paused, and repeat offenders get a much longer time-out. Choose Relaxed, Balanced or Strict with one click.
  • Instant lockout for bot usernames — “admin”, “root” and friends lock a bot out on the first try, unless someone on your site really uses that name.
  • Never lock me out — one click adds your own address to the allow list.
  • Allow and deny lists — single addresses, ranges and wildcards.
  • Activity log — every sign-in, wrong password, lockout and block, with the Brain’s verdict, search, filters and CSV export.
  • Invisible bot trap and generic error messages — bots cannot tell whether a username exists.
  • Hardening — block username discovery, switch off XML-RPC and pingbacks.
  • Email alerts — when someone is locked out, and (optionally) when a person signs in from a browser and network they have never used.
  • Cloudflare and proxy support — reads the real visitor address, safely.
  • A recovery switch — add DFLS_DISABLE_LOCKOUTS to wp-config.php and nobody is locked out until you remove it.

Privacy

Everything the Brain knows stays in your WordPress database. Nothing is sent to DadsFam, to an AI company or to any other service — the free plugin makes no outside requests at all.

It stores, per person, the browsers they have signed in with (as a random token matched by a scrambled fingerprint) and the networks they use (as one-way fingerprints that cannot be turned back into addresses). A recognised browser gets one first-party cookie, dfls_tb, which only your site can read. The activity log keeps the address, username and browser name of each attempt for 30 days by default. Uninstalling the plugin removes all of it.

Pro features (DadsFam Login Security Pro add-on)

Two-factor codes, a smart sign-in check that asks for an email code when a sign-in looks unusual to the Brain, a CAPTCHA, a hidden login address, breached-password checks, country blocking, sessions control and a full audit trail.

A word about PRO

Right, let me be straight with you, because I hate being sold to as much as you do.

Everything above is free and it stays free. The lockouts, the allow and deny lists, the activity log, the live dashboard, the email alerts, the bot traps and the hardening — none of those are premium features. Those are the things a login-security plugin should just do, and if I put them behind a paywall I would be taking the mickey.

There is a PRO add-on. It exists because I am a dad in Cape Town, and this is one of the things that puts food on the table at my house. That is the honest reason. Not “unlock your potential”, not “supercharge your workflow”. Just: if this plugin kept the bots off your login page and you can spare it, PRO helps me keep building.

What PRO adds is the second layer you reach for once the door is already locked — two-factor codes, a CAPTCHA, a hidden login address, breached-password checks, country blocking. That is extra security and convenience. It is not the plugin working properly, because the plugin already works properly.

So if the free one does everything you need, brilliant. Genuinely. Use it, and I hope your activity log stays boring. If you get to the point where a second factor or a hidden login would let you sleep better, PRO is at plugins.dadsfam.co.za.

Either way, thanks for using something I built. — Zak, DadsFam

PostcodeEU
PostcodeAPI
Pro6PP
Nederland Postcode
Postcode Connect

plugins.name: DineKit – Restaurant Menu, Online Ordering, Table Reservations & POS
plugins.author: weblevelup
plugins.short_description: Run your restaurant on WordPress — menus & allergens, online ordering, table bookings and card payments. Commission-free, no monthly fees.
plugins.description:
DineKit turns WordPress into a complete, commission-free restaurant platform — menus, online ordering, table bookings and card payments — with nothing to pay per cover, per order or per month. You bring your own Stripe account and keep 100% of every sale.

Menus & allergens

  • Menu builder — menus (Lunch, Dinner, Drinks…), sections and dishes with photos, badges and multiple prices; drag-and-drop ordering with autosave.
  • Seven designer templates, one click apart — each built for a venue type: Signature (the modern default), Maison for fine dining, Counter for fast-casual, Noir for evening menus and bars, Bistro, Fresh for cafés and brunch, Mono for minimalists. The Fraunces display font ships inside the plugin — no external font services.
  • Design Studio — click any part of the live menu preview to style exactly that element: per-element text sizes, colours and corner rounding, updating live as you drag. Your accent colour carries over to the Order Online page automatically, so everything matches your brand.
  • UK-14 allergens built in — the 14 regulated allergens pre-loaded with icons, tooltips, sub-sources (e.g. “cereals containing gluten → wheat, barley”) and a printable matrix (Natasha’s Law friendly), plus your own custom allergens and dietary labels. Declare “may contain” traces separately — quieter badges on the menu, ± in the matrix, and diners avoiding an allergen also avoid traces of it.
  • Bulk-edit in a spreadsheet — export the whole menu to CSV, tweak prices and dishes in Excel or Google Sheets, re-import to update everything at once (never duplicates).
  • Costs, margins & calories — record a dish’s cost to make and see its gross-profit margin (kept private), and show calories on the public menu for UK calorie-labelling.
  • QR table cards and A4 posters that open your live menu on a phone, and Menu / MenuItem / LocalBusiness schema.org output for SEO.
  • Opening hours with holiday overrides and a live “open now” status.

Online ordering

  • Takeaway, collection and delivery ordering with a diner-facing menu, dish customizations (removable ingredients, choose-your-options with prices) and an accept / hold / refund workflow that only captures payment when you accept.
  • A live orders board — new orders appear by themselves (no refreshing) with a count in the browser tab; every order carries a “where’s it from” badge with a channel filter; history is day-scoped and searchable by date; phone orders are keyed in on a fast POS-style pad.
  • Pre-orders days ahead — optionally let diners order for later in the week: a Day picker at checkout, only your real opening hours offered, kitchen capacity respected per day, and scheduled orders held in their own group until you accept.
  • Per-slot capacity — cap how many online orders each time slot can take so a rush never swamps the pass; full slots grey out in the diner’s picker.
  • Contactless QR “order at the table” so diners order from their phone — straight onto that table’s tab, or pay-upfront.
  • Kitchen Display (KDS) — a live New → Preparing → Ready board for the kitchen, with per-ticket timers, item lists and notes, one-tap advance and a full-screen mode for any tablet or kitchen TV.
  • Kitchen & bar ticket routing — printable tickets per station, or emailed directly to a kitchen printer on accept.
  • 86 a dish in one tap — sold-out dishes stay on the menu (SEO-safe) marked unavailable and can’t be ordered anywhere.
  • Branded, editable email templates for order and booking notifications, with a live preview.

Point of sale — Take Order

  • A real POS for dine-in service, in any browser on any tablet — no proprietary hardware, nothing to lease.
  • Live floor plan that reads your diary — Take Order opens on your real room layout: every table colour-coded by how long it’s been seated (green → amber → red against your turn time) with its stage (Seated → Ordered → Cooking → Served), parties seated from the bookings diary lit before they’ve even ordered, reserved-soon warnings on free tables (“free until 22:00”), and settled tables flagged for clearing. Starting an order on a free table books the walk-in into the diary automatically — every screen tells the same story.
  • The till knows the guest — open a table and see who’s sitting there: name, VIP flag, allergies, and their standing notes (“always tops up the wine”), pulled from the same guest record the diary uses.
  • Tabs with coursing — build each table’s order and fire courses in rounds; firing confirms exactly what’s being sent and takes a ticket note (“allergy at seat 2”) that shows on the Kitchen Display and prints on station tickets.
  • Bill splitting — evenly, by item, or partial payments; service charge and tips.
  • Every tender — cash with change calculation, card via a Stripe smart reader, pay-by-QR from the guest’s phone, vouchers and comps; manager-gated voids.
  • Mistakes are fixable — pressed voucher but meant cash? Wrong amount? A manager can change a payment’s method in place, remove a mis-keyed payment (the tab reopens to settle correctly) or reopen a tab settled by accident — every amend logged, so the books always tally.
  • Keeps working when the internet drops — carry on opening tables, adding rounds, firing to the kitchen and taking cash through an outage. Everything is held on the tablet and syncs itself the moment you’re back, with nothing lost and nothing charged twice.
  • Cash-up with opening float and X/Z reports at close.
  • Loyalty built in — members earn points on spend and redeem them as a bill discount.

Bookings & events

  • Commission-free table reservations — take bookings on a drag-and-drop floor plan with joinable tables, via a public reservation form (block + [dinekit_booking] shortcode) with live availability, waitlist and covers-per-hour pacing, deposits, and a booking diary with email notifications and printable slips. Repeat no-shows get a red flag so you can ask for a deposit.
  • Full-width service timeline — the whole service at a glance with a live “now” line and the past greyed out; drag a booking exactly where you want it, click to seat or edit. Walk-ins are a one-tap popup with the best-fit table pre-selected.
  • Set-menu events with per-guest pre-orders via a share link — guests choose their courses and flag allergens; the kitchen gets a consolidated prep sheet.

Payments, guests & staff

  • Card payments with your own Stripe keys (encrypted at rest) — booking deposits, order payments and at-the-table card-present payments via Stripe smart readers, with Apple Pay and Google Pay. You keep 100%.
  • Unified guest CRM — one profile per guest across bookings, orders and loyalty: lifetime spend, visits, average order, allergies, VIP flag, service notes and past no-shows — shown on the Guests screen, on every booking, and at the till.
  • Staff rota & labour — build the week’s rota in colour-coded role bands: split shifts, automatic unpaid-break deduction, day-off and sick markers, holiday requests approved right on the rota, contracted-hours warnings and a live labour-cost total. Today and tomorrow highlight themselves; copying a day copies the whole day.
  • Text messages via your own Twilio (beta) — booking confirmations, automatic reminders, “your table is ready” and “order ready for collection”; bring your own Twilio account, pay their raw prices, every switch off by default (see External Services). Write your own message wording with placeholders like {name} and {time}, with a live preview; on a paid Twilio account, UK venues can send from their restaurant’s name instead of buying a number.
  • Staff logins with a role-to-permission matrix and an activity/audit log, plus review-request emails to win diners back.
  • Reports — covers, revenue, best-selling dishes and no-show rate, with CSV export.
  • GDPR-ready — WordPress’s Export / Erase Personal Data tools cover everything DineKit stores, with anonymised financial records kept for your accounts.
  • Direct support from your dashboard — message the DineKit team without leaving WordPress (optional; see External Services).

Install it as an app on any phone or tablet — the staff app runs from its own home-screen icon, keeps taking orders and cash even when the internet drops (syncing itself once you’re back), and many tablets stay in sync automatically (an order or booking made on one appears on the others within seconds).

No WooCommerce required and no page builder needed. The menu, allergens and QR codes work with no external accounts; card payments use your own Stripe account (see External Services below). Works with any theme, on any host.

Built by Web Level Up, a UK web agency that builds commercial WordPress software.

External services

DineKit’s optional payments feature (booking deposits and online order payments) uses Stripe to take card payments. Stripe is contacted only after you enable it and enter your own Stripe API keys under DineKit → Integrations, and only on requests that involve a payment:

  • When a diner pays, DineKit asks Stripe to create a payment by sending the amount, currency, your site URL and the related booking/order reference to Stripe’s API (https://api.stripe.com).
  • When you connect Stripe or set up its webhook, DineKit calls Stripe to validate your keys and register payment notifications.
  • On pages where a payment can be made, Stripe’s official Stripe.js library is loaded from https://js.stripe.com so card details are entered directly with Stripe and never reach your server (PCI SAQ-A).

If you do not enable payments, DineKit makes no external requests. Stripe is a third-party service; by using it you agree to Stripe’s terms and privacy policy:

  • Terms: https://stripe.com/legal
  • Privacy: https://stripe.com/privacy

DineKit’s optional text message (SMS) feature uses Twilio, with your own Twilio account and credentials (DineKit → Integrations → Text messages). Twilio is contacted only when SMS is enabled and a notification you turned on actually fires (a booking confirmation or reminder, a “table ready” tap, or a collection order marked ready): DineKit sends the recipient’s phone number and the message text to Twilio’s API (https://api.twilio.com) so Twilio can deliver the text. Your Twilio auth token is stored encrypted on your own site. If you do not set up SMS, Twilio is never contacted. Twilio is a third-party service; by using it you agree to Twilio’s terms and privacy policy:

  • Terms: https://www.twilio.com/en-us/legal/tos
  • Privacy: https://www.twilio.com/en-us/legal/privacy

DineKit’s optional direct support feature (DineKit → Support) sends your support request to Web Level Up, the makers of DineKit, at https://weblevelup.co.uk. If you have never used Support, this service is never contacted:

  • When you send a request or reply, DineKit transmits the name, email address, subject and message you typed, plus your site address (used to link replies back to your dashboard and keep your ticket history together).
  • If — and only if — you tick the “include my site details” box, your WordPress, PHP and DineKit version numbers are attached to help with debugging.
  • Opening the Support screen fetches your own site’s ticket history from the same service.
  • Once you HAVE made a support request, DineKit periodically checks that same service for replies to your own requests (roughly every 10 minutes, sending only your site’s support token) so the notification bell can tell you when the team has answered. No other data is sent, and the check stops entirely if you uninstall or never had a request.

If you prefer not to use direct support, the Support screen also links to the plugin’s free forum at https://wordpress.org/support/plugin/dinekit/ — using the forum sends nothing to Web Level Up. Web Level Up privacy policy: https://weblevelup.co.uk/privacy-policy/

When you deactivate DineKit, an optional questionnaire asks why, so a free plugin can learn what it got wrong. Answering is entirely voluntary and nothing is sent unless you choose an answer and press “Send & deactivate” — choosing “Skip & deactivate” contacts nobody, and deactivation always goes ahead either way. If you do send it, DineKit transmits to Web Level Up at https://weblevelup.co.uk: the answer you picked and anything you typed in the box; your DineKit, WordPress and PHP version numbers; and how far you got with the plugin (days installed, and how many menus, dishes, orders and bookings you had — counts only, never your menu content, your customers or your takings). Your email address and site address are included only if you tick “You can email me about this”. The dialog lists all of this before you send. Web Level Up privacy policy: https://weblevelup.co.uk/privacy-policy/

Development

DineKit is open source (GPLv2+). The complete human-readable source — including the React admin application and the build tooling used to generate the bundled dist/main.js — is publicly available and maintained at:

https://github.com/nikutx/dinekit

To build the admin app from source: npm install then npm run build (Vite). See the repository README for the full development setup.

plugins.name: PublisherKits SocialPromoter
plugins.author: PublisherKits
plugins.short_description: Post and schedule social media promotions from WordPress Posts directly to X, LinkedIn, Facebook and Bluesky.
plugins.description:
SocialPromoter by PublisherKits lets publishers post and schedule social media content from WordPress Posts directly to X (Twitter), LinkedIn, Facebook Pages and Bluesky — without leaving the editor.

Core features (free — everything in this plugin is fully functional):

  • Write social copy with a live character counter (280-character X warning)
  • Click post tags to insert as hashtags
  • Post Now — fires immediately to all selected accounts
  • Schedule — pick a date and time, WP Cron handles the rest
  • Queue view — see all upcoming scheduled posts and cancel any
  • Post history — the full, paginated log of everything sent, with errors
  • Multiple accounts per platform — ideal for agencies and multi-brand publishers
  • Brand hashtags — standing tags blended into every post

Pro features — supplied in a separate package; their implementation is not included in this WordPress.org build:

  • Engagement statistics — likes, comments, shares and clicks on sent posts
  • Campaigns — group posts, UTM-tag every link, PDF/GA4 client reports
  • Automation — new-post suggestions, reposting and story boosts
  • AI copy drafting — tone, goal and technique variants
  • Branded images — platform-sized canvases with your logo and headline bar
  • WP Job Manager support — post and schedule from job listings
  • Author tagging — writers’ handles and hashtags suggested automatically, stored in BioBuilder-compatible fields so the two stay in sync
  • Assisted posting — for places that will not accept a post from an app, LinkedIn and Facebook groups among them. SocialPromoter does not post to those on your behalf and neither does anything else: both platforms closed group posting to third-party apps. What it does instead is everything up to the send — writes the copy, prepares the image, holds it until the moment you chose, then reminds you and hands it over with one-click copy and a link straight to the destination. You paste; it records that you posted it

Supported platforms:

  • X (Twitter) — OAuth 1.0a, posts via API v2
  • LinkedIn — personal profiles and company pages
  • Facebook — pages (requires Facebook developer app)
  • Bluesky — app-password login, posts with clickable links

X and Facebook use your own developer app credentials. LinkedIn uses the shared PublisherKits relay app so company-page posting can use the approved LinkedIn Community Management API access.

More from PublisherKits

SocialPromoter is one of a small range of tools built for people who actually run publications. Each works on its own, and all are free on WordPress.org:

  • PublisherKits BioBuilder – stop leaving author profiles blank. When a post is published, BioBuilder finds the author’s professional profile and fills in their bio, social handles, job title and employer.
  • PublisherKits ExcerptBuilder – AI-powered excerpt generation using the WordPress AI Client. Write, rewrite or tidy excerpts on demand, or auto-draft them on publish for review.
  • PublisherKits PluginTidy – works out which plugins your site actually uses, records every plugin change, and makes removing one safe.

External Services

This plugin connects to the following external APIs when you have configured credentials and connected accounts:

  • X API (api.twitter.com and upload.twitter.com) — for OAuth authentication, posting tweets and uploading post images. Your post text, link and image are sent when you post; your app credentials are sent when authenticating. X Developer Terms of Service | X Privacy Policy
  • Facebook Graph API (graph.facebook.com) — for OAuth authentication and posting to Facebook Pages. Your post text, link and image are sent when you post; your app credentials are sent when authenticating. Meta Platform Terms | Meta Privacy Policy
  • LinkedIn API (api.linkedin.com) — for OAuth authentication and posting shares. Your post text, link and image are sent when you post. LinkedIn API Terms of Use | LinkedIn Privacy Policy
  • Bluesky API (bsky.social) — for app-password authentication and posting. Your post text, link and image are sent when you post. Bluesky Terms of Service | Bluesky Privacy Policy

  • PublisherKits LinkedIn connect relay (pkits.org) — LinkedIn connections are authorised through a shared PublisherKits developer app, so you do not need your own LinkedIn developer app. The relay is operated by us (PublisherKits, Black and White Trading Ltd) and is contacted in two situations. During the connect step: when you click Connect, your browser is sent to LinkedIn to sign in, and your site then posts a one-time ticket, a nonce and a signature to the relay to complete the OAuth handshake and receive the LinkedIn access token, which is stored encrypted on your own site. And to renew access: LinkedIn access expires after about 60 days, so up to once a day (and when a post finds access already expired) your site posts the connection’s stored LinkedIn refresh token and your site’s host name to the relay, which exchanges it with LinkedIn for a new access token and returns it; the relay does not store or log either token. No post content, personal data or analytics is ever sent to the relay; posts go directly from your site to api.linkedin.com. PublisherKits Terms of Service | PublisherKits Privacy Policy

  • PublisherKits Support Copilot service (bwtlsupport.com) — optional in-plugin support assistant, the Help button on SocialPromoter admin screens. When you use it, your question and recent chat history are sent, together with your site address and (where available) its licence installation identifier used to authorise the request and apply fair-use limits, the plugin version and those of other installed PublisherKits plugins, the admin screen name, and a short whitelist of non-sensitive settings and counts (which social platforms have a connected account, how many accounts and how many queued, sent and failed posts exist, and five on/off settings covering reminders, queue auto-cancel, debug logging and uninstall clean-up). No account names or handles, access tokens, API keys, post copy or scheduled-post content are ever sent, and the assistant is read-only — it cannot change anything on your site. Nothing is sent until a user who can manage this plugin’s settings accepts the in-widget privacy notice; consent can be withdrawn on the Support screen. Ordinary questions are not retained after they are answered. Only if you open the ticket form (“Send to support” or “Still need to raise a ticket?”) and click “Create ticket” does the plugin send the conversation (up to its 20 most recent messages), the site details, settings and counts above, the question category, the contact email address you enter (pre-filled with your WordPress account email) and the first and last name from your WordPress user profile; these are kept, to become a support ticket. PublisherKits Terms of Service | PublisherKits Privacy Policy

No data is sent to these services until you have configured app credentials and connected accounts. Posting only occurs when you explicitly click Post Now or approve a scheduled post. The Support Copilot sends nothing until its privacy notice is accepted.

This plugin also uses the Freemius SDK (freemius.com) for licensing, updates and optional usage diagnostics. No data is sent to Freemius unless you explicitly opt in on the activation screen — skipping the opt-in keeps the plugin fully functional. Freemius Terms of Service | Freemius Privacy Policy

This free plugin makes no AI requests: AI copy drafting belongs to the separately distributed Pro version, which uses the AI provider the site configures in WordPress core’s Settings > Connectors, under that provider’s own terms and privacy policy.

plugins.name: CrossPeak OMS for WooCommerce
plugins.author: CrossPeak
plugins.short_description: Easy eCommerce Order Management
plugins.description:
This plugin integrates your existing WooCommerce store with CrossPeak OMS.

plugins.name: Trill AI Product Chat for WooCommerce

plugins.short_description: Free AI shopping assistant for WooCommerce that turns chat into measurable revenue. Cart-aware, verified order tracking, GDPR-ready. No API key.
plugins.description:
Trill AI Product Chat for WooCommerce — the AI shopping assistant that turns chat into measurable revenue.

Trill AI Chat Lite adds a friendly, store-aware AI chat to your WooCommerce site in under 5 minutes. Robin — the AI assistant — answers shoppers in natural language using your real catalogue, your real page content, the current cart, and verified order data. The merchant gets a dashboard that proves revenue from chat. Free forever, open source, GDPR-ready.

New in 2.4 — GDPR tools that usually sit behind a paywall, free

  • GDPR Tools admin page. Look up everything the plugin holds for a visitor’s email, review it on screen, download it as JSON or CSV, or erase it permanently — with a typed DELETE confirmation so nothing is removed by accident.
  • Audit trail. Every search, view, export and erase is recorded: who, when, and how many records. Emails are stored masked — and there is deliberately no IP column, because I never store IPs.
  • Consent gate in the widget. Optionally require visitors to accept your privacy notice before chatting. Consent lives only in their browser and is re-requested automatically if you change the notice.
  • “Request My Data” in the widget. Visitors can trigger a WordPress-native personal-data request straight from the chat footer, confirmed by email through WordPress core.
  • Retention dashboard. See stored totals and your retention window at a glance, preview what a cleanup would delete, or run it on demand.

New in 2.3 — resilient by design

  • Reinstall without fear. Deleting and reinstalling the plugin now reconnects to Trill Cloud automatically — the plugin proves it controls your site and receives a fresh connection secret. Your plan and monthly usage are preserved.
  • Small catalogues get real answers. “What do you sell?” now responds with your featured and latest products instead of coming up empty.
  • Policy questions find the right policy. Answers draw from a wider variety of your pages — one snippet per page — so “what’s your refund policy?” surfaces the Refund page every time.
  • An honest usage bar. The Monthly Usage panel shows your plan’s real allowance (50 free / 2,000 on Trill Cloud) and updates automatically when your plan changes.

New in 2.2 — see every conversation

  • New Conversations admin page. Browse every chat from a new Trill Chat → Conversations screen, with message count, average rating, conversion status and attributed revenue on every row.
  • Filter and search. Narrow by date range, status and star rating, and search across message content to find any conversation fast.
  • Read full transcripts. Open any conversation in a popup to read the complete back-and-forth, rendered as plain text.
  • Export to CSV. Download the whole filtered list, or a single conversation’s transcript — exports are hardened against spreadsheet formula injection.
  • Tidy up. Permanently delete conversations you no longer need, one at a time or in bulk.

Why store owners pick Trill AI Chat over generic AI plugins

  • WooCommerce-native, not bolted on. Understands products, variations, stock, categories, carts and orders out of the box — every code path is designed for e-commerce.
  • 5-minute install. No API keys. No external account signup — your WordPress admin is the only login you need.
  • Reads your real catalogue + your real pages. Real-time product search and page content indexing. Robin can answer “do you have red dresses?” and “what’s your return policy?” from the same conversation.
  • Knows the cart. Robin sees what shoppers already added and helps them checkout instead of forgetting state.
  • Privacy-first order lookup. Identity verified before any order detail is shared. WordPress login for registered customers, email-match for guests, silent fall-through on mismatch.
  • Revenue attribution built in. Orders placed within 24h of a chat are tagged as “from chat” and surface on the dashboard with attributed revenue.
  • Managed AI, predictable cost. Generous monthly conversation allowance on Trill Cloud. Track usage from the admin dashboard. No OpenAI account required.
  • Topic-safe. Built-in guardrails auto-generated from your store metadata keep conversations about shopping, politely declining homework, code generation, medical or legal advice.
  • Prompt-injection-protected. The assistant will not reveal system instructions or adopt different personas.
  • GDPR-ready, with the tooling to prove it. UK-registered company (Greensolutions Pioneers Limited, Companies House 15693716). HTTPS end-to-end. Chat data is never used to train AI models. A dedicated GDPR Tools page covers access, portability and erasure — audited, and with no IPs ever stored.
  • Fast. Sub-second responses on typical product questions.

What Lite includes (free, forever)

  • AI shopping assistant widget on every page of your store
  • Smart product discovery — real-time catalogue search with natural-language understanding (50+ shopping phrases, English de-pluralisation) and product cards with one-click AJAX add-to-cart
  • Page content indexing — Robin also answers from your FAQ, shipping, returns, contact and policy pages
  • Cart-aware chat that sees the current basket and guides to checkout
  • Verified order tracking with login or email-match identity check
  • Smart lead capture for out-of-stock and price-drop opt-ins, with audited consent
  • Revenue analytics dashboard — orders and revenue attributed to chat, 7/30/90-day windows
  • Conversation history — browse, filter, full-text search, read, export (CSV) and delete every chat
  • Full GDPR toolkit — data subject lookup, on-screen access, JSON/CSV portability and audited erasure from a dedicated admin page; widget consent gate and “Request My Data”; DSAR + erasure via WP Privacy Tools; configurable retention with preview and run-now
  • Topic-safe — guardrails and prompt-injection protection keep chats about your store
  • Full widget customisation — colours, position, size, assistant name, avatar, font, starter chips and privacy notice, with live preview
  • WooCommerce-ready — WordPress 6.0+, WooCommerce 8.0+ and HPOS compatible; [trill_chat] shortcode to embed anywhere
  • Built to extend — translation-ready (.pot, Loco Translate, WPML) and the WordPress 7.0 Abilities API for AI agents and MCP adapters
  • Generous monthly conversation quota on Trill Cloud, tracked in the dashboard

Need more conversations? Trill Cloud

The free tier includes 50 conversations per month — plenty to see the value on a smaller store. Growing stores can upgrade to Trill Cloud (£12/month) for 2,000 conversations per month, longer AI responses and priority support. The upgrade is applied to your site’s existing connection — same plugin, no reinstall — and the dashboard usage bar reflects your new allowance automatically. See trillai.io/pricing.

Built for WooCommerce, by a UK developer

I build Trill AI at Greensolutions Pioneers Limited, a UK-registered company (Companies House 15693716). I focus exclusively on AI products for WooCommerce — not a generic chatbot with a Woo plugin bolted on.

If you run a UK, US or EU store and want AI chat that respects your data, your time and your budget, I’d love to hear what you think.

Read more on the Trill AI blog:

  • Complete guide to AI chat for WooCommerce
  • Reduce WooCommerce support tickets with AI
  • WooCommerce AI chat vs live chat

Developer-friendly

Clean PSR-4 architecture, WordPress coding standards, filter hooks for customisation (trcl_localize_script_data), and debug logging via WP_DEBUG. No Composer dependencies, no external JavaScript libraries.

External Services

This plugin relies on Trill Cloud, the managed AI back-end I operate
(Greensolutions Pioneers Limited), at https://api-v2.trillai.io, as its sole
AI processing service. The service is required for the plugin to function.

What data is sent, and when:

  • When a store visitor sends a chat message, the message text and the
    WooCommerce context needed to answer it — product names, prices, descriptions
    and, where relevant to the question, the current cart contents and order-status
    details — are transmitted to Trill Cloud over HTTPS for AI processing.
  • Each site authenticates with a per-site Bearer token (hashed at rest). Trill
    Cloud enforces the monthly conversation allowance server-side (no local
    trialware).
  • No IP addresses are sent, and no customer personal data beyond what the
    visitor types into the chat and the catalogue context required to answer.

Service links:

  • Service URL: https://api-v2.trillai.io
  • Terms of Service: https://trillai.io/terms-of-service/
  • Privacy Policy: https://trillai.io/privacy-policy/

No personal visitor data is collected or stored by Trill Cloud beyond what is
strictly necessary to process each individual chat message. Chat data is never
used to train AI models.

plugins.name: Rebel Studios Brazilian Checkout Fields for WooCommerce
plugins.author: rebelstudios
plugins.short_description: CPF, CNPJ and CEP fields for WooCommerce in Brazil: check-digit validation, address and company autofill, and the data on orders, emails and the API.
plugins.description:
Rebel Studios Brazilian Checkout Fields adds the fields a Brazilian store needs to the WooCommerce checkout — CPF, CNPJ, company legal name (Razão Social), RG, state registration (Inscrição Estadual), street number and neighbourhood (bairro) — and does three things that are usually missing:

  1. Real validation. CPF and CNPJ are checked against the official check digits, in the browser and on the server. An invalid document never reaches the order.
  2. Autofill. Type the CEP and the street, neighbourhood, city and state fill in. Type the CNPJ and the company’s legal name and address come with it.
  3. The data goes where you need it. CPF, CNPJ and legal name appear on the order screen, in emails and in the REST API — ready for your invoicing (NF-e) integration. Collecting a document you cannot use later is the problem this plugin exists to solve.

The plugin’s interface is in Brazilian Portuguese. It is fully internationalized (i18n), so it can be translated into any language through translate.wordpress.org once published.

Every field is optional

Each field has three states: Disabled, Optional or Required. A store that sells digital products does not need to ask for a CPF; one that invoices companies needs a CNPJ and legal name and nothing else. You decide, without touching code.

Works with both checkouts

Compatible with the WooCommerce classic checkout and the block checkout, and with HPOS (High-Performance Order Storage). Data is stored the same way by both checkouts, so an invoicing integration only has to read one format.

On the block checkout, customers choose between individual (Pessoa Física) and company (Pessoa Jurídica), and see only the documents for that choice.

Privacy and reliability

CEP and CNPJ lookups are made from your server, not from the customer’s browser, and are cached. If a lookup service is down, the customer simply types the address — a purchase is never blocked by a third-party API.

External services

To fill an address from a postcode and a company from its registration number, this plugin sends the value the customer typed to two free, public Brazilian services. Every request is made from your server (never the customer’s browser), only when a customer enters a CEP or a CNPJ, and the response is cached on your site so the same value is not looked up twice. No data is ever sent to the makers of this plugin.

ViaCEP (https://viacep.com.br/)
Used to turn a Brazilian postcode into a street address. When a customer types an 8-digit CEP, that CEP — and nothing else — is sent to ViaCEP, which returns the street, neighbourhood, city and state. No personal data (name, email, document number) is sent. ViaCEP is a free public service that does not publish a separate terms-of-service or privacy-policy page; its usage information is on its website: https://viacep.com.br/.

BrasilAPI (https://brasilapi.com.br/)
Used to turn a company registration number into the company’s public details. When a customer types a 14-digit CNPJ (a public company registration number, not personal data), that CNPJ — and nothing else — is sent to BrasilAPI, which returns the company’s public registration data (legal name and registered address). BrasilAPI is a free, open-source community project. Its terms of use are published on its site: https://brasilapi.com.br/#termos-de-uso . It does not publish a separate privacy-policy page; the project and its source are documented at https://brasilapi.com.br/ .

The Diagnostics panel on the settings screen also sends one sample request to each service (at most once every 5 minutes) to show whether it is responding. It uses a fixed example CEP and CNPJ, never customer data.
